text:
sylvia.park: Heads up — onboarding the new eu-north-1 GPU nodepools is failing during scale-up. Nodes keep stuck in Pending with kubelet logs showing no secondary IPs available for ENI attachment.

omar: Seen it. Autoscaler started 6 nodes, kubelet created pods, then crashloop when CNI couldn't allocate a secondary address.

raj: Is this the same subnet we reserved last week? I thought we asked for a /22 for GPU subnets.

sylvia.park: We have a /24 for the GPU subnet (internal mistake). The estimate was off because each GPU node group uses multiple ENIs and secondary IPs for pods (we're using aws-cni with custom networking).

infra-bot: Incident created: infra-1767894321. Notifying cloud-ops and oncall.

cloud-ops: Adding context — on this account the current per-subnet assignable IPv4 pool is ~250 (after AWS reserved addresses). With ENI+secondary IP per node we need ~400 to support burst.

maria: Are we hitting Elastic IP limits too? Some of the control-plane NAT nodes need stable external IPs.

omar: Control plane EIPs are fine. This is purely per-subnet secondary IP exhaustion (assignable IPs for pods/nodes). EIP quotas are separate.

luke: Can we temporarily scale down the nodegroups and move some GPU jobs to a different region? We have spare capacity in eu-west-1 but that means cross-region data movement for canaries.

raj: Short-term mitigation: reduce max pods per node (kubelet flag) to free secondary addresses. Long-term we need either larger subnet (request /22) or enable IPv6 for pod addressing to avoid IPv4 exhaustion.

omar: I filed a quota request to AWS to increase VPC subnet size (support case 012345678901234). Also requested per-subnet assignable IP headroom via account team. Response ETA: 48-72h.

gcp-support: FYI tagged the AWS case and sent an internal ops escalation to the cloud rep — asked for expedited review citing production node failures.

maria: If we switch to IPv6 for pod IPs we need to audit all external integrations that assume IPv4. That's a nontrivial roll.

sylvia.park: Agreed. IPv6 is mid-term. For now we need a hotfix plan we can apply in the next 2 hours. Suggestions?

luke: Hotfix plan: 1) scale down noncritical GPU nodegroups by 30% 2) patch autoscaler to prefer eu-west-1 for new evicted jobs 3) adjust maxPods to 60 on GPU nodes (reduces per-node secondary IP consumption) 4) add preflight check in cluster-provisioner to validate assignable IPs before creating nodepool

raj: +1. I can push a patch to cluster-provisioner to fail fast when assignable_ip_count < predicted_needed. Quick code snippet: 

```
# pseudo
if assignable_ips < expected_nodes * ips_per_node:
  abort("insufficient assignable IPs for nodepool")
```

omar: Implemented step 1 and 3 now. Scaling noncritical pools down. Monitoring pods to see if Pending clears.

infra-bot: Autoscaler event: reduced desired count on ng-gpu-batch from 20 -> 14 (requested by omar).

maria: Cloud support replied to case 012345678901234 — AWS says can't change subnet mask after creation; recommended creating a new larger subnet and migrating. ETA for expedited feedback: 24h.

sylvia.park: Migration path: create new /22 in same AZs, create nodepools there, cordon+drain old nodes, migrate workloads. That works but takes ~3-4h to ramp and may disrupt canaries.

gcp-support: Also suggested enabling 'assignSecondaryIpAddress' tuning at CNI level to reduce host-level ENI usage — could be a quick config change in CNI daemonset, low-risk.

raj: Let's do both: apply CNI tuning (low risk, immediate), then create the new subnet and nodepools in parallel. I'll open an infra change and schedule a maintenance window.

luke: I'll take migration runbook and coordinate with product for canary freeze.

maria: Documenting cost impact — creating new /22 and additional ENIs temporarily increases hourly network IP allocations and we might see small uptick in NAT gateway EIP usage. Budget estimate ~ +$1.2k/month while both subnets active.

omar: Monitoring shows pending pods dropping after reducing maxPods and scaling down noncritical pools. We'll continue with CNI tuning and start new subnet prep.

sylvia.park: Thanks everyone. Action items: raj (open change + CNI tune), luke (migration runbook & canary coordination), omar (monitor + keep scaling adjustments), maria (track cost estimate & update billing owner). I'll follow up when support case updates. :thumbsup:
